title: Sweep a servo
instructions:
## A motor that goes where you tell it

An RC servo on pin 9 moves to the angle you write (0 to 180 degrees). The `Servo` library hides the pulse timing: `myServo.attach(9)` then `myServo.write(angle)`.

## Do this

Make the servo sweep from 0° to 180° and back in steps of 10°, waiting 100 ms between steps so the horn can follow. The checks look for the servo reaching 0°, 90° and 180°.
hints: for (int angle = 0; angle <= 180; angle += 10) { myServo.write(angle); delay(100); }
Then a second loop counting down from 180 to 0.
Servo is a class: declare it once outside setup() and loop().
realityNote: A hobby servo expects a 1 to 2 ms pulse every 20 ms; the library generates it with a timer. Servos draw a surge of current when they move, so power them from a separate 5 V supply with a common ground, not from the board's regulator.
